finalText:
The current revision is **NIST SP 800-63B-4**. I read it at https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html. The page is dated "Tue, 26 Aug 2025", and its abstract says "This publication supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B." I searched the page for "draft", and the only hits were references to other documents, so this is not a public draft. The CSRC publication page (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/63/b/4/final) returned a 404, so I couldn't check the revision status there. I didn't open the older Rev 3 page, so I make no claims comparing the two.

All password requirements are in Sec. 3.1.1.2, "Password Verifiers", on https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html:

- **Single-factor minimum length: SHALL, 15 characters.** The same item says verifiers MAY allow shorter passwords that are only used in multi-factor authentication, but SHALL still require at least eight characters.
- **Maximum length: SHOULD, at least 64 characters.** Verifiers should permit passwords of at least this length.
- **Composition rules: SHALL NOT.** Verifiers must not require mixes of character types.
- **Periodic change: SHALL NOT.** However, verifiers SHALL force a change if there is evidence of compromise.
- **Password hints: SHALL NOT.** Hints that unauthenticated claimants can see are not allowed.
- **Security questions: SHALL NOT.** Verifiers must not prompt for knowledge-based authentication or security questions when a password is chosen.
- **Blocklist: SHALL.** Verifiers must compare a new password against a blocklist of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords. They must compare the whole password and give the reason for any rejection.
- **Password managers: SHALL.** Verifiers must allow password managers and autofill. They SHOULD also allow pasting.
- **Salt length: SHALL, at least 32 bits.**
- **Hashing scheme: SHOULD, not SHALL as the plan expected.** The page says an approved scheme from the latest revision of SP 800-132 (or updated NIST guidance) "SHOULD be used". The separate rule that passwords be salted and hashed with a "suitable" scheme is a SHALL.
